2. Background facts
The informant, in this case, is the mother of the victim girl.

The case of the prosecution, which emerges from the report and other materials, is that the elder daughter of the informant, on the date of the incident i.e. 04.07.2017, was studying in 2nd standard at Zilha Parishad School.

The accused/appellant- Vilas Nikore is the nephew of Lahanuji.
The appellant, a resident of village Asole, used to frequently come to the house of his maternal uncle.
The informant and her daughters were acquainted with him.
It is stated that on 04.07.2017 at 5:00 p.m. there was a dindi/procession of lord Vitthal in the village.
The informant went to the procession with her daughters and mother-in-law.
After performing pooja, the informant came back leaving her two daughters with her mother-in-law.
Her husband was at home.

At about 6:30 p.m.,
the victim came back home.
She was crying.
On being questioned by the informant, she said that she was thirsty and therefore, she was coming back home.
On the way, the appellant caught hold her and took her in his house.
He kissed her and tried to give her Rs.10/-.
She did not accept the same.
It is stated that thereafter the appellant removed her knickers and kissed her private part.
It is stated that the victim told her mother that he put some foreign article in her private part and therefore, she had a pain.
When she cried, the appellant released her.
The appellant, after releasing her, threatened her 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt not to disclose the incident to anyone.
The victim was experiencing serious pain in her private part.
The informant examined her private part and found that there was a swelling on her private part.
The informant and her husband took the victim to the house of the appellant, which was shown by the victim girl.
They entered into the house.

The victim pointed towards the appellant,
being the perpetrator of the crime.
The father of the victim went to the police patil and informed him about the incident.
The villagers went in search of the appellant.
The informant lodged the report at Nandgaon Khandeshwar police station.
3. On the basis of the report, a crime bearing No. 168 of 2017 was registered against the appellant/accused.
PW-5 Avinash Palave, the then SDPO, Amravati, carried out the investigation.
He visited the spot and drew the spot panchanama.

sentences.text: 8. In this case, the victim girl on the date of the incident was seven years old.
The victim girl in her evidence has stated that her birth date is 19.03.2010.
She has stated that 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt she was studying in 2nd standard.
PW-2-Sheetal Dandekar is the mother of the victim girl.
She has stated that she has two daughters.
Her elder daughter was 13 years old and her younger daughter (the victim girl) was 10 years old on the date of her evidence i.e. on 28.10.2021.
PW-2, the mother of the victim, has stated that the birth date of the victim is 19.03.2010.
PW-1 and PW-2 were subjected to searching cross- examination on all other aspects except the age and birth date of the victim.
The appellant has not challenged the age of the victim as well as the birth date of the victim.
9. The prosecution has produced the photocopy of the birth certificate of the victim girl.
It is marked as Article 'G'.
The investigating officer had collected the bona fide certificate of the victim girl from the Zilha Parishad school, Bori.
It is at Exh. 37.
The appellant has not challenged this document.
It is apparent that the investigating officer during the course of the investigation had produced a photocopy of the birth certificate.

Perusal of the record would show that the prosecution did not 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt examine any other witness or produce other documentary evidence inasmuch as the appellant did not deny the birth date and age of the victim.
The evidence adduced by the prosecution is sufficient to prove that on the date of the incident, the victim was 7 years of age.
The learned Judge has properly appreciated the evidence adduced by the prosecution to prove the age of the victim.
I do not see any reason to discard and disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the prosecution to prove the age of the victim.
This evidence is sufficient to prove that the victim girl was 7 years of age on the date of the incident.

Since the appellant has not challenged the oral and documentary evidence, it would be appropriate to place reliance on the bona fide certificate at Exh.
37.
In the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, the document at Exh. 37 cannot be eschewed from consideration.
The admissibility of the document in evidence was not challenged.
The victim girl was seven years of age.
In view of this, the contents of this document fully support the case of the prosecution.
Since the accused has not challenged this 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt document, no inference can be drawn against the case of the prosecution.
Therefore, it is clear that the victim on the date of the incident was below 12 years of age.

10. It is the case of the prosecution that when the victim girl was returning after attending the Lord Vitthal procession, the appellant overpowered her and dragged her in the house of his maternal uncle and committed this offence.
It is the case of the prosecution that the appellant has committed penetrative sexual assault by inserting something in her private part.

12.
It is to be noted that the incident occurred on 04.07.2017 at about 5:30 p.m.
The report was lodged on 05.07.2017 at 1:30 a.m.
It has come on record that after meeting police patil, the informant, her husband and the victim went to the Nandgaon Police station and lodged the report.
The report was promptly lodged.
In this case, the prompt lodging of the report reflects upon the credibility of the victim girl and the informant.
Perusal of the record does not show that the report was embellished in any manner.
I am satisfied that this report was not out of sheer imagination and concoction.
The informant did not exaggerate the incident.
In my view, this is a very vital circumstance in favour of the case of the prosecution.
There was no enmity or dispute between the informant and the appellant.
He was visiting his maternal uncle's place.
There was no motive for lodging the false report 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt against the appellant.
It is to be noted that reporting of such a matter to the police with certainty invites stigmatic consequences not only for the victim girl but also for the family.
The reputation of the family and girl is at stake.
The reporting of such matter not only defame the family, but also humiliates and causes unimaginable embarrassment to the family.
In this case, the parents of the victim displayed exemplary courage to report this incident to the police without wasting any time.
In my view, this reflects upon the credibility and truthfulness of the testimony of the victim and the informant.
I do not see any reason to discard and disbelieve their evidence as to the occurrence of the incident.
13. The victim and the informant have stated that the appellant had inserted something in her private part.
The victim has not stated that the appellant had inserted his finger in her private part.
Similarly, she has not stated that he had inserted any foreign article in her private part.
It is not the case, either of the victim or the informant, that the appellant 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt committed the penetrative sexual assault.
In this context, it would be necessary to appreciate the evidence of the medical officer.
The victim was referred for medical examination on 05.07.2017.
PW-3 Dr. Sushama Shendre examined the victim on 05.07.2017 at 5:30 p.m.
The history of the assault was narrated by the mother of the victim.
The medical certificate at Exh. 47 shows that the history of the assault narrated by the mother of the victim was recorded by the medical officer.
The history of the assault narrated by the informant and recorded in the report at Exh. 47 is consistent with the account of the incident stated by the informant as well as stated by the victim girl.
The medical officer on local examination did not notice injuries to the private part of the victim.
Her hymen was intact.
The medical officer did not notice injuries on her body as well.
The medical officer has stated in the report that she could not give an exact opinion.

It is seen that the medical officer at the time of the examination of the victim did not notice any swelling or change Vilas S/O Ramesh Nikokre vs The State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Nandgaon ... on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53090698/

sentences.text: The evidence of the medical officer does not corroborate the 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt
evidence of PW-1 and 2 with regard to the insertion of any article or a finger in the vagina of the victim.
If there was a fingering of the vagina by the appellant, then there would have been some injury to the genitals of the victim.
The absence of the injury in the factual situation is the most important circumstance to rule out the penetrative sexual assault.
14. The next important issue is as to whether this evidence is sufficient to prove the offence of a rape/the offence of a penetrative sexual assault on the victim.
The victim has stated that the appellant removed her knickers and kissed her private part.
She has also stated that the appellant also removed his undergarments.
He laid her on the cot and thereafter, she felt that the appellant had inserted something in place of her urine.
The mother of the victim has stated that the victim told her that the appellant had removed her knickers and kissed her private part.
In my view, this evidence of the victim and her mother cannot be discarded.
I do not see any reason to discard and disbelieve the evidence of the victim and her mother that 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt
the appellant in the course of this incident kissed the vagina of the victim.
In this context, it would be necessary to consider Section 3(d) of the POCSO Act.

It reads thus :
"3. Penetrative sexual assault- A person is said to commit "penetrative sexual assault"

(d) he applies his mouth to the penis, vagina, anus, urethra of the child or makes the child to do so to such person or any other person.

Section 375(d) of the IPC reads thus:
"375 Rape - A man is said to commit "rape" if he- (a) ....................................................
(b) .......................................................

First - Against her will.
Secondly - Without her consent.
Thirdly- With her consent when her consent has been obtained by putting her or any person in whom she is interested, in fear of death or of hurt.
Fourthly - With her consent, when the man 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt knows that he is not her husband and that her consent is given because she believes that he is another man to whom she is or believes herself to be lawfully married.

sentences.text: Applying the mouth to the vagina falls within the definition of rape as defined under Section 375(d) of the IPC as well as under Section 3(d) of the POCSO Act.
Therefore, the appellant cannot be given the benefit of the doubt.
The evidence is sufficient to prove this fact.
The victim on the date of the incident was below 12 years of age.
This offence proved against the appellant is punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt the IPC.

The victim was below 12 years of age on the date of the crime and therefore, the offence proved against the appellant would be aggravated penetrative sexual assault under Section 5(m) of the POCSO Act punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
The offence was committed on 04.07.2017.

The learned judge, on conviction, has sentenced the appellant to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of the IPC and further sentenced the appellant to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years for the offence punishable under Section 4 of the POCSO Act.
In my view, this sentence of 20 years awarded under Section 4 of the POCSO Act was not in accordance with the law.
The offence proved against the appellant would be under Section 5(m) punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
Section 6 provides the punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.

The same was the position as far as the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of the IPC is concerned.
17. It is therefore apparent that the minimum sentence provided was 10 years rigorous imprisonment.
The learned Judge has proceeded on the assumption that the mandatory sentence of 20 years will have to be awarded in view of the mandate of Section 4 of the POCSO Act.

In my view,
the conviction of the appellant under Section 4 of the POCSO Act was itself illegal inasmuch as the victim on the date of the penetrative sexual assault was below 12 years of age.
Therefore, conviction under Section 4 cannot be sustained.
18. The learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that the old-aged parents of the appellant are dependent on him.
The appellant on the date of the commission of the offence was 29 years old.
He is a poor labour.
He is unmarried.
It is submitted that his old-aged parents are suffering 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt unimaginable hardship.
It is therefore submitted that while awarding the sentence for the proved offence the leniency may be shown to the appellant.
The learned APP submitted that considering the age of the victim and the nature of the offence proved against the appellant, the maximum sentence is required to be awarded.
19. I have given thoughtful consideration to the submissions.
It is seen on perusal of the judgment and order that the learned judge has not considered the provision of Section 42 of the POCSO Act while awarding the sentence.

As per this section, where an act or omission constitutes an offence under the POCSO Act and also under Section 376 of the IPC, the offender found guilty shall be liable to punishment under the POCSO Act or under the IPC, as provides for punishment which is greater in degree.
In this case, the punishment provided is similar.

Therefore, the punishment of ten (10)
years of rigorous imprisonment under Section 376(2)(i)
would be sufficient.

It would not be necessary to award the separate 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt sentence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
20.

In the facts and circumstances, in my view, keeping in mind the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the appellant, it would be just and proper to convict the appellant for the offence under Section 5(m) of the POCSO Act and sentence him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years.
In my view, this punishment would be proportionate to the gravity of the crime.
The appellant, by this time, might have reflected over the wrong committed by him and repented over the same.
In my view, ten (10) years of rigorous imprisonment would meet the ends of justice.
21. Accordingly, the criminal appeal is partly allowed.
22. The judgment and order of conviction of the appellant/accused dated 06.05.2022 is modified.

Vilas S/O Ramesh Nikokre vs The State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps
Nandgaon ... on 11 December, 2024
Author: G. A. Sanap
Bench: G. A. Sanap
2024:Bhc-Nag:14251
 210.Cri.Apeal 887
 1
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Nagpur Bench, Nagpur.
CRIMINAL APPEAL (APEAL) NO. 887 OF 2022
Vilas S/o. Ramesh Nikore,
 Aged about : 33 yrs, Occu.: Labour  R/o. Aasole, Tq. Near Parsopant,
 Dist. Yavatmal  (Presently at Central Prison, Amravati) 
 // V E R S U S //
 The State of Maharashtra,
 Through P.S.O., P.S. Nandgaon,
 Khandeshwar, Distt. Amravati.
..
 -----------------------------------------------------------------------
Mr G. D. Kale, Advocate (appointed) for the appellant  Mr Piyush Pendke, APP for the respondent/State
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
 CORAM : G. A. SANAP, J.
DATE : 11/12/2024 OR A L JUDGMENT :
1. In this appeal, challenge is to the judgment and order dated 06.05.2022 passed by the learned Special Judge and Additional Sessions Judge-2, Amravati (for short 'the learned Judge'), whereby the learned Judge convicted the appellant/accused for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'the IPC') and for 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt the offence punishable under Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'the POCSO Act')
and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for ten (10) years and to pay a Vilas S/O Ramesh Nikokre vs The State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Nandgaon ...
opennyai_summary.facts:
On Vilas S/O Ramesh Nikokre vs The State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Nandgaon ...
4. The learned Judge framed the charge against the appellant.
The appellant pleaded not guilty.
The learned Judge,
on consideration of the evidence, held the appellant guilty of the above offences and sentenced him as above.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The victim girl was tutored to depose against the appellant.
The evidence of the victim is not credible and trustworthy.
The evidence of the victim girl has not been supported by the medical evidence.
The learned Advocate submitted that if a finger or any other article was inserted in the vagina, then there ought to have been some injury to the genitals of the victim.
The doctor has ruled out the possibility of the penetrative sexual assault.
In the absence of cogent and concrete evidence of the age of the victim, the learned Judge was not justified in holding the appellant guilty of the charge under the POCSO Act.
7. The learned APP submitted that the offence of penetrative sexual assault as defined under Section 3(d) of the POCSO has been made out.
The learned APP submitted that even if it is assumed for the sake of argument that the injuries were not noticed by the medical officer at the time of examination, the evidence of the victim that the appellant kissed her private part and inserted some article in her private part is sufficient to hold the appellant guilty of the offence of rape as defined under Section 375(d) of the IPC and Section 3(d) of the POCSO Act.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Perusal of the record would show that the prosecution did not 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt examine any other witness or produce other documentary evidence inasmuch as the appellant did not deny the birth date and age of the victim.
The evidence adduced by the prosecution is sufficient to prove that on the date of the incident, the victim was 7 years of age.
The learned Judge has properly appreciated the evidence adduced by the prosecution to prove the age of the victim.
This evidence is sufficient to prove that the victim girl was 7 years of age on the date of the incident.
The victim girl was seven years of age.
Since the accused has not challenged this 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt document, no inference can be drawn against the case of the prosecution.
Therefore, it is clear that the victim on the date of the incident was below 12 years of age.
It is the case of the prosecution that the appellant has committed penetrative sexual assault by inserting something in her private part.
The reporting of such matter not only defame the family, but also humiliates and causes unimaginable embarrassment to the family.
If there was a fingering of the vagina by the appellant, then there would have been some injury to the genitals of the victim.
The absence of the injury in the factual situation is the most important circumstance to rule out the penetrative sexual assault.
Applying the mouth to the vagina falls within the definition of rape as defined under Section 375(d) of the IPC as well as under Section 3(d) of the POCSO Act.
Therefore, the appellant cannot be given the benefit of the doubt.
The victim on the date of the incident was below 12 years of age.
This offence proved against the appellant is punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt the IPC.
The victim was below 12 years of age on the date of the crime and therefore, the offence proved against the appellant would be aggravated penetrative sexual assault under Section 5(m) of the POCSO Act punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
The offence was committed on 04.07.2017.
The learned judge, on conviction, has sentenced the appellant to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of the IPC and further sentenced the appellant to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years for the offence punishable under Section 4 of the POCSO Act.
In my view, this sentence of 20 years awarded under Section 4 of the POCSO Act was not in accordance with the law.
The offence proved against the appellant would be under Section 5(m) punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
In my view,
the conviction of the appellant under Section 4 of the POCSO Act was itself illegal inasmuch as the victim on the date of the penetrative sexual assault was below 12 years of age.
It is seen on perusal of the judgment and order that the learned judge has not considered the provision of Section 42 of the POCSO Act while awarding the sentence.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Prior to the amendment of Section 6 with effect from 16.08.2019, the punishment for aggravated penetrative Vilas S/O Ramesh Nikokre vs The State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Nandgaon ...
Therefore, the punishment of ten (10)
years of rigorous imprisonment under Section 376(2)(i)
It would not be necessary to award the separate 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt sentence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
20.
In my view, ten (10) years of rigorous imprisonment would meet the ends of justice.
21. Accordingly, the criminal appeal is partly allowed.
22. The judgment and order of conviction of the appellant/accused dated 06.05.2022 is modified.
The accused/appellant - Vilas Ramesh Nikore is 210.Cri.Apeal 887.2022.judge.odt acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
24. The conviction of the accused/appellant - Vilas Ramesh Nikore for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code is maintained.
In addition to this, he is convicted for the offence under Section 5(m) punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
25. The appellant is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for ten (10) years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine he is further sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for two months for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code.
26. No separate sentence is awarded for the offence under Section 5(m) punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
The High Court Legal Services Sub Committee, Nagpur is directed to pay the fee of the learned appointed Advocate, as per the rules.
28. The criminal appeal stand disposed of, accordingly.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
